---
title: "Results"
---

There were 2,491 baseline blood samples assayed for 799,149 CpG sites (Illumina EPIC array) from participants of the population-based prospective Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study (AGES-RS, mean age 76 y) [@RN1]. As a part of the extensive phenotyping, assessment of dementia was included in the baseline and 5-yr repeat exam (2003-2011), and vital status and dementia status was followed in administrative and health records since baseline for up to 13.4 years (end 2015). The study cohort included 161 participants with baseline prevalent dementia (follow-up = 0 days), stable normal with no subsequent report of dementia (n = 1,581, follow-up = 3,869 days) and four prospective transition groups: baseline normal to mild cognitive impairment with no subsequent report of dementia (normal2mci, n = 99, follow-up = 1,921 days), stable MCI with no subsequent report of dementia (stable_mci, n = 49, follow-up = 2,104 days), normal to incident dementia (normal2incid, n = 494, follow-up = 2,730 days), and MCI to incident dementia (mci2incid, n = 107, follow-up = 2,239 days) (@tbl-dementia-category). Of the total number of MCI diagnoses — a portion transitioned from normal to MCI (38.8%), remained stable from baseline to end-of-follow-up (19.2%), and a group transitioned from baseline MCI to dementia (41.9%). Briefly, with each dementia group ordered by clinical severity, mean age of the sample increased, and years of education were lower. The sex distribution was generally 43% males and 57% females, with different proportions in the stable_mci and normal2incid groups. Performance on 3 cognitive tests declined over the groups; on average, the cognitive test scores of the MCI-involved groups were lower than stable normal (Supplementary Table [-@supptbl-covariate]–[-@supptbl-baseline]).

### Stages exhibit distinct methylation patterns

We quantified the covariate adjusted effect size of the association between each CpG site (methylation differences of M-values) and each transition stage or prevalent dementia relative to the stable-normal group (reference, @supptbl-exemplar). There were 403 significant CpG sites (*P* < 1.0 × 10⁻⁸). Of these 403, there were 5 DMPs in the normal2mci, 62 in the stable_mci, 1 in the normal2incid transition, 9 in the mci2incid transition, and 326 in the prevalent dementia groups respectively (@suppdata-DMP403). These CpG sites were distributed across the whole genome, many of which are associated with genes that are critical for neurologic function (@suppfig-manhattan).

We then investigated the pairwise directionality and correlations of the DMP effect size between dementia groups, controlling for covariates. We found strong positive effect size correlations between prevalent dementia and the prospective dementia transition groups normal2incid (*r* = 0.87, *P* = 0, exceeding machine precision limits) and mci2incid (*r* = 0.86, *P* = 0) (@fig-normal2mci a). However, the DMP effect sizes compared to the normal2mci group were negative (*r* = -0.48, *P* = 0; @fig-normal2mci a). These patterns persisted in the subjects who at baseline either had mild cognitive impairments (@fig-normal2mci b, mci2incid transition) or were cognitively normal (@suppfig-normal2incid_DMP, normal2incid transition) but later developed dementia.
We also investigated the pairwise correlations by incorporating additional CpG sites using less stringent thresholds (*P* < 1.0 × 10⁻⁷, threshold 7; *P* < 1.0 × 10⁻⁶, threshold 6; *P* < 1.0 × 10⁻⁵, threshold 5) (@fig-normal2mci c-d, Supplementary Fig. [-@suppfig-normal2incid_extended_DMP]–[-@suppfig-mci2incid_extended_DMP]) and across the range of *P* value thresholds from *P* < 1.0 × 10⁰ to *P* < 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰, similar results were found (@fig-normal2mci e-f, @suppfig-ES_corr_mci2incid_normal2mci).

The stable_mci group exhibited a distinctive methylation pattern. While the majority of the DMPs (main group, n = 343, stable_mci effect size > -0.2) showed the same correlations described above — positive with prevalent dementia (*r* = 0.68, *P* = 0), normal2incid (*r* = 0.71, *P* = 0) and mci2incid (*r* = 0.63, *P* = 0), and negative with normal2mci (*r* = -0.43, *P* = 0) (@suppfig-stable_mci_DMP) — it also carried an overhanging outlier group (n = 60, stable_mci effect size < -0.2) whose effect sizes were near zero in every other group and uncorrelated with every transition (|*r*| ≤ 0.21, *P* ≥ 0.11; @suppfig-stable_mci_DMP). This dichotomy persisted when additional CpG sites were included at less stringent thresholds (Supplementary Fig. [-@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_prev]–[-@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_transitions]).

### Latent dimensions discriminate dementia stages

The preceding EWAS analysis examined individual DMP sites and did not model the underlying interdependencies among CpG sites. To capture the inherent clustering of DMP sites in relation to dementia group, we performed dimension reduction analyses using two complementary approaches, variational autoencoder (VAE) (@suppfig-vae-methodology) and UMAP, which summarise the data in different ways. VAE is a probabilistic generative model that learns a distribution over the methylation features, with each latent dimension capturing a distinct axis of variation that separates dementia groups. UMAP instead summarises the spatial topography of the CpG data, placing subjects with similar epigenetic profiles close together in a low-dimensional space whose number of dimensions is set as a model parameter.

Both approaches used the same set of 403 DMP sites (*P* < 1.0 × 10⁻⁸; THR8) and, to capture sites of suggestive significance, the 949 CpG sites that passed the *P* < 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ threshold (THR7). At THR8, latent values differed most between the prevalent dementia group and the stable normal group: four of the six VAE dimensions distinguished the two (criterion of *P* < 1.0 × 10⁻², t-test), with VAE_2 (*P* = 4.18 × 10⁻²⁶), VAE_6 (*P* = 4.88 × 10⁻²⁶) and VAE_4 (*P* = 5.82 × 10⁻¹⁵) lower and VAE_3 (*P* = 3.12 × 10⁻³) higher in prevalent dementia (@fig-vae-boxplots a). The stable_mci group, by contrast, was barely distinguishable from stable normal, with no VAE dimension reaching significance (@fig-vae-boxplots b). Both patterns held at THR7: VAE_1 (*P* = 1.44 × 10⁻²⁴) and VAE_2 (*P* = 1.58 × 10⁻¹⁷) again separated prevalent dementia from stable normal, while stable_mci remained indistinguishable (@suppfig-vae-boxplot-t7).

We next asked whether these latent values changed progressively as groups became increasingly more demented, ordering the six dementia groups by baseline status and subsequent trajectory: normal2mci, stable_normal, stable_mci, normal2incid, mci2incid, and prevalent dementia. The magnitude of the latent values tracked this clinical course, decreasing near-monotonically along the ordering in VAE_6 (*P* = 5.88 × 10⁻³⁰, ANOVA), VAE_2 (*P* = 2.02 × 10⁻²⁹) and VAE_4 (*P* = 3.75 × 10⁻¹⁷) (@fig-vae-boxplots c). The same gradient reappeared at THR7 in VAE_1 (*P* = 2.01 × 10⁻²⁷) and VAE_2 (*P* = 2.05 × 10⁻¹⁸), the two dimensions reaching significance at that threshold (@suppfig-vae-boxplot-one-dim-t7).

UMAP recovered the same structure. Its dimensions again separated prevalent dementia from stable normal most strongly, while stable_mci stayed close to stable normal (@suppfig-umap-boxplot-t8 for THR8 and @suppfig-umap-boxplot-t7 for THR7), and selected UMAP dimensions likewise changed gradually across the progression ordering (@fig-vae-boxplots d for THR8; @suppfig-umap-boxplot-one-dim-t7 for THR7).

### Latent dimension pairs reveal progression trajectory

We next examined how pairs of latent dimensions moved together across the dementia stages, using two-dimensional kernel density contours of the 403 DMP sites (*P* < 1.0 × 10⁻⁸; THR8) to show where subjects with similar epigenetic profiles clustered (VAE, @fig-scatter-peak a,b; UMAP, @fig-scatter-peak c,d). The clusters shifted gradually in latent space as groups became more demented: for UMAP_1 and UMAP_5, subjects migrated from the lower left toward the upper right along the ordering from normal2mci to prevalent dementia (@fig-scatter-peak c). Connecting the per-group cluster centers traced a continuous path across the stages (@fig-scatter-peak e,f for VAE and g,h for UMAP), and the same transition appeared across additional VAE pairs (@suppfig-vae-scatter-t8-p1) and UMAP pairs (Supplementary Fig. [-@suppfig-umap-scatter-t8-p1]–[-@suppfig-umap-scatter-t8-p2]).

We quantified this shift with the dementia progression score (DPS), which measures how closely the sequence of per-group contour centroids follows the clinical dementia ordering (see Methods; +1 if the centroids lie on a straight line in the correct order, −1 for the reversed order, and 0 for no progression). The six latent dimensions formed 15 pairs, ranked by DPS. The top VAE pairs reached DPS values of 0.442 and 0.415 (@fig-scatter-peak e,f) and the top UMAP pairs 0.911 and 0.834 (@fig-scatter-peak g,h). At THR8, permutation testing (1,000 iterations) confirmed 10 UMAP pairs and 9 VAE pairs as significant (all *P* < 0.05; Supplementary Fig. [-@suppfig-vae-null-dist]–[-@suppfig-perm-heatmap]); at THR7 the significant UMAP pairs rose to 14 while VAE held at 9 (@suppfig-perm-heatmap).

The two methods differed for the stable_mci group: VAE placed its centroid off the progression path (@fig-scatter-peak e,f, @suppfig-vae-scatter-t8-p1), whereas UMAP kept it on the path (@fig-scatter-peak g,h, Supplementary Fig. [-@suppfig-umap-scatter-t8-p1]–[-@suppfig-umap-scatter-t8-p2]). This may reflect the VAE capturing the overhanging outlier group of stable_mci CpG sites (Supplementary Fig. [-@suppfig-stable_mci_DMP]–[-@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_transitions]).

### APOE genotype effects on DNA methylation patterns

We next asked whether these latent epigenetic patterns differed among persons with different APOE genotypes, which reflect susceptibility to Alzheimer's dementia. Genotype was associated with dementia in this cohort (chi-square *P* = 4.18 × 10⁻¹³; @supptbl-apoe-dementia). We grouped the six genotypes by functional role — protective (ε2/ε2, ε2/ε3), neutral (ε3/ε3), and detrimental (ε2/ε4, ε3/ε4, ε4/ε4) — and tested each latent dimension for a difference across these roles (Kruskal-Wallis test); six of the twelve dimensions differed significantly at THR8 (403 CpGs; @fig-apoe-boxplots). Two UMAP dimensions, UMAP_5 (*P* = 0.00084) and UMAP_1 (*P* = 0.0014), had the lowest values in protective genotypes, rose slightly in the neutral genotype, and rose further in the detrimental genotypes; UMAP_2 (*P* = 0.00997) showed the inverse trend, higher in protective and lower in detrimental genotypes. Of three significant VAE dimensions, VAE_6 (*P* = 0.00318) and VAE_2 (*P* = 0.00423) decreased steadily from protective to detrimental genotypes, while VAE_4 (*P* = 0.0147) followed the same direction more weakly. At THR7 (949 CpGs), five dimensions differed by role (@suppfig-apoe-boxplot-t7): UMAP_2 was again higher in protective genotypes, whereas UMAP_1, UMAP_3, and VAE_1 increased toward the detrimental genotypes and VAE_2 differed only marginally, with overall separation weaker than at THR8.

### Concordance of individual DMPs with other studies

We assessed the reproducibility of effect sizes describing the association of dementia group to DMP site by comparing AGES results to 3 independent studies: the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) and the Australian Imaging, Biomarkers, and Lifestyle (AIBL) cohorts summarized in a meta-analysis (META) [@RN44], and the AddNeuroMed study [@RN24] (@supptbl-reference-comparison). We selected from META 96 CpG sites (*P* < 1.0 × 10⁻⁴·⁵) associated with AD (vs cognitively normal (CN) control) and compared those effect sizes to the same DMP sites in relation to AGES. We found moderate but significant correlations for prevalent dementia (*r* = 0.47, *P* = 7.06 × 10⁻⁶) and for the transition stages progressing to dementia, mci2incid (*r* = 0.52, *P* = 6.74 × 10⁻⁷) and normal2incid (*r* = 0.42, *P* = 7.76 × 10⁻⁵) (@fig-validation a; reference group: stable normal). Relaxing the threshold to 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ increased the number of CpG sites to 224, with concordance remaining robust (*r* = 0.46, 0.37, and 0.36; *P* = 5.71 × 10⁻¹², 5.7 × 10⁻⁸, and 1.8 × 10⁻⁷ for prevalent dementia, mci2incid, and normal2incid, respectively) (@fig-validation a).

AddNeuroMed reported effect sizes for MCI and for AD, each relative to CN controls. Both comparisons correlated consistently with the AGES effect sizes for normal2incid, mci2incid, and prevalent dementia (*r* = 0.16 to 0.44; @fig-validation b). Directionality tests indicated that a significant number of DMP sites had concordant effect-size directions between AGES and META — at every selection threshold for normal2incid and mci2incid, and at all but the most stringent one for prevalent dementia (@fig-validation c) — or between AGES and AddNeuroMed, for all three AGES groups in both the AD and the MCI comparison (@fig-validation d).

### Biological pathway analysis reveals stage-specific biological processes

We conducted a pathway analysis to identify biological processes that could contribute to different stages of dementia. The number of CpG sites passing the genome-wide significance threshold was highly uneven across the five dementia groups — normal2mci (n = 5), stable_mci (n = 62), normal2incid (n = 1), mci2incid (n = 9), and prevalent dementia (n = 326) (@suppfig-pval-with-top-genes, @suppdata-DMP403) — too uneven for a balanced enrichment comparison. We therefore selected the top 1,000 CpG sites ranked by EWAS *P*-value for each group. Gene annotation yielded comparable numbers of associated genes: normal2mci (n = 1,474), stable_mci (n = 1,447), normal2incid (n = 1,530), mci2incid (n = 1,534), and prevalent dementia (n = 1,566) (@fig-pathway-analysis a, Supplementary Data [-@suppdata-CG_normal2mci]–[-@suppdata-CG_prev]). Despite these comparable gene counts, Gene Ontology (GO) biological process (BP) enrichment differed markedly across the groups: normal2mci yielded the most enriched GO BP terms (n = 155), more than three times as many as mci2incid (n = 48) and seven times as many as prevalent dementia (n = 22). Most of these terms were stage-specific — 140 of 155 (90%) were unique to normal2mci, 9 of 12 (75%) to stable_mci, 16 of 18 (89%) to normal2incid, 30 of 48 (63%) to mci2incid, and 14 of 22 (64%) to prevalent dementia (@fig-pathway-analysis b, @suppdata-GO_top1000). In the top 2,000 CpG sites, normal2mci again yielded both the most enriched GO BP terms (n = 354) and the most stage-specific ones (n = 202), although the stage-specific fraction fell in every group (@suppfig-upset-top2000, @suppdata-GO_top2000).

We then grouped the enriched GO BP terms into functional categories (@fig-pathway-analysis c, Supplementary Table [-@supptbl-top1000-normal2mci]–[-@supptbl-top1000-prev]). The normal2mci transition was enriched for ion transport and regulation (13 BP terms), synaptic function and organization (8 BP terms), and extracellular matrix organization (7 BP terms). The stable_mci group was uniquely enriched for hypoxia response (3 BP terms) and regulatory mechanisms (2 BP terms), the mci2incid transition for hormone signaling (5 BP terms) and cell migration and organization (7 BP terms), and prevalent dementia for cell-cycle regulation (3 BP terms). The normal2incid and mci2incid transitions shared two functional categories, both related to neurodevelopmental processes: development and differentiation, and neural development and regulation. These stage-specific patterns were reproduced in the top 2,000 CpG sites (@suppfig-barplot-top2000).
